We walk through the plan and the schedule with you before any work starts, so you know what to expect and how long the room will be out of use. In Sedona's high-UV, low-humidity, freeze-thaw climate, cedar and redwood both perform well, but they behave differently over time. Cedar is often the smarter choice for most local pergola projects because it balances beauty, availability, cost, and stability. Redwood can be a strong premium option for highly visible outdoor spaces or when matching existing architecture. The bigger detail many homeowners miss is finish strategy. In our climate, both cedar and redwood need the right penetrating oil finish and a realistic maintenance plan if you want the structure to age well.
